intro: Everyone you sell to, people and companies, with what each owes and when they last bought. Follow your deals through a pipeline, keep track of calls and visits, gather customers into lists, and reward them with loyalty points.
start: Add your customers with New customer, or bring them in at once with Import CSV.
Set a credit limit and payment terms for the customers who buy on credit.
Make a pipeline with the stages your sales go through, then add your open deals.
Turn on the loyalty scheme if you want invoices to earn points.

articles.title: Add a customer
articles.summary: Add a person or an organisation. One that looks like a customer you already have is pointed out before you save.

steps.rest: Under Who is the customer?, choose A person or An organisation.
For a person, their name, email and phone. For an organisation, its legal name as on its registration, which is printed on every invoice.
for an organisation, if you have it. It is checked with the tax office after you save.

steps.rest: if it appears. Open the match if it is the same customer, or press Add anyway.

steps.lead: Press Add the person or Make the organisation.
steps.rest: They can be chosen on quotations and invoices at once. Nothing is shared with the customer.

tips: Import CSV adds many customers at once and names any rows it refused. Export gives you the list back as a file.
Stage says how far along they are: lead, prospect or customer.

articles.title: Merge a customer entered twice
articles.summary: Move everything from the duplicate to the customer you keep, then remove the duplicate. It cannot be undone.

steps.lead: Open the customer you want to keep
steps.rest: and press Merge a duplicate.

Its documents, activities, lists, tickets and loyalty points become this customer's.

steps.lead: Confirm with Merge, and the duplicate's name, in.
steps.rest: The duplicate is removed. Press Keep them apart instead if they are different customers.

articles.title: Remind customers who are late paying
articles.summary: Tick the customers on the list and send their overdue invoice reminders in one go.

articles.summary: A column for each stage, with what its deals are worth. Add a deal and move it on as it goes.

articles.title: Gather customers into a list
articles.summary: Make a list of customers you want to reach together, ready for a campaign.

steps.rest: give it a name and what it is for, and press Make the list.

steps.lead: Choose the list and press Add customers.
steps.rest: Find a customer by name, phone or email, and press Add.

tips: Take off removes someone from the list. They stay a customer.
A campaign's audience can be chosen from your lists.

articles.title: Reward customers with loyalty points
articles.summary: One switch, two numbers: invoices earn points, and customers may pay in them. Tiers reward those who earn most.

steps.rest: and switch on Invoices earn points, and customers may pay in them.

steps.lead: Enter the points for each unit spent
steps.rest: and what a point is worth when spent, then press Save. The example shows the rule in words.
to add a level such as silver or gold, with the points a member needs to reach it, and press Make the tier.
after changing tiers, to place every member in the highest tier their earned points reach.

tips: Points are earned when an invoice for a member is posted, on its amount before tax, once per invoice.
Voiding the invoice takes the points back.
A customer can pay a receipt in points. With too few, it is refused.

articles.title: Enrol a customer and change their points
articles.summary: Add a customer to the scheme in a tier, and adjust their points by hand with a reason.
before: Turn the scheme on and make at least one tier first.

steps.rest: on Members.

steps.lead: Choose the customer and a tier,
steps.rest: then press Enrol the customer. They earn from their next posted invoice.
to give or take points by hand. Use a minus to take them.

steps.lead: Say why and press Adjust the points.
steps.rest: The reason is kept on the Points ledger with every other change.

tips: An adjustment is the only way points change by hand.
Points ledger shows every point a member earned, spent or was given, and why.
